# Intent: Disk Steward macOS evidence monitor

A macOS user can leave Disk Steward running as a lightweight menu-bar app, understand material disk growth, export trustworthy evidence for Codex or Claude, and query the same evidence through a read-only local MCP integration.

## Success Evidence

- `REQ-001` — A signed-development build launches as a menu-bar utility; left-click opens a compact status board and right-click exposes Export, Settings, About, and Quit.
- `REQ-002` — The app measures whole-volume capacity while collecting bounded detailed evidence for configured roots and registered agent process trees.
- `REQ-003` — Evidence identifies path, time, size delta, actor and agent session when observable, and labels exact, tool-linked, inferred, or unknown attribution without guessing.
- `REQ-004` — A user can export a portable, integrity-manifested evidence bundle containing a concise Codex brief and machine-readable detailed records.
- `REQ-005` — Codex and Claude can query sanitized evidence through the same read-only local MCP executable without rescanning the disk.
- `REQ-006` — Monitoring remains useful without restricted privileges and enables exact Endpoint Security provenance only when entitlement and user authorization are available.
- `REQ-007` — The app records no file contents, provides explicit privacy exclusions and retention limits, and performs no deletion or cleanup mutation in this intent.
- `REQ-008` — Automated and reproducible checks demonstrate buildability, evidence correctness, regression safety, bounded idle resource use, and recovery from unavailable monitoring components.

## Constraints

- Use a native Swift-first macOS architecture and keep the continuously running footprint bounded.
- Prefer macOS 13 or newer, Swift 6, AppKit for status-item mouse behavior, SwiftUI for presented UI, SQLite for local evidence, and the official Swift MCP SDK.
- Treat Endpoint Security entitlement approval as an external dependency and preserve a functional FSEvents/snapshot fallback.
- Keep MCP read-only and avoid an externally reachable HTTP listener.
- Do not persist file contents, secrets, or unbounded raw write-event streams.
- Every attribution statement must carry method and confidence.
- Generated evidence and databases must have deterministic retention and size controls.

## Non-Goals

- Automatic deletion, cache purging, process termination, or destructive MCP tools.
- Cloud synchronization, accounts, telemetry, or a hosted backend.
- Windows or Linux support.
- Detailed monitoring of external, network, Time Machine, or cloud-placeholder volumes by default.
- Reading or classifying file contents.
- Guaranteeing Apple Endpoint Security entitlement approval.

## Assumptions

- `ASM-001` (medium) — The development machine has a compatible Xcode and Swift toolchain for a macOS 13+ Swift 6 application.
- `ASM-002` (medium) — A native project layout can package the menu app, a local MCP executable, and later a system extension without introducing a second application language.
- `ASM-003` (high) — Endpoint Security entitlement may be unavailable or delayed, so exact system-wide attribution cannot be a prerequisite for the standard product path.
- `ASM-004` (high) — A stdio MCP executable can serve both Codex and Claude while delegating sanitized queries to the local app-owned evidence service.
